html:
The Sabirs were a nomadic, probably Turkic, people of the North Caucasus steppe, from the late 400s to the 600s. On the map for 700 they sit between the Kuban and the Caspian.

Byzantine writers say they were skilled warriors with a large army that included women, that they built siege engines and boats, and that some called them Huns. In the wars between the Byzantine Empire and the Sasanian Empire in the 500s, Sabir groups fought for both sides. By the 600s they had come under the rising Khazars. Some scholars think the Huns of the Caucasus were part of them.
